findings.what: The string viewer crashes when a start is safe but its line, its ends or the legal play from it passes 2^53. inArithmetic picks SafeInt when every typed entry is safe. stringView only checks that `top` is safe, so stringThrough, fire (the two ends) and play (the in-orbit test) then throw EngineOverflow inside the $derived `view`. Opened from a link, the island never hydrates: data-hydrated stays empty, every control stays disabled, no notice is shown, and the static A2 default stays on screen under a bar that holds the link. With a typed start, the board shows the new numbers beside a stale line, and later moves do nothing.
findings.evidence: scratch specs/near.spec.ts against the built site on port 7720. ?g=A2&k=1&c=n&s=5,9007199254740990 gave pageerror 'element 2 of the string at node position 0 has the entry 9007199254740992, which is not a safe integer', hydrated null, enabledControls 0, notice 0, line ['1,0','-1,1']. s=1,9007199254740991, s=9007199254740991,9007199254740991 ('mul gave 18014398509481982') and s=4503599627370496,4503599627370496 also left hydrated null. ?g=G2&k=1&c=n&s=3,3002399751580330 and ?g=A2&k=2&c=n&s=9007199254740991,1 hydrated with an empty string-viewer board (values []). Typing 5, 9007199254740990 and pressing Set gave the same pageerror and line ['1,0','-1,1']; a click on node 2 afterwards left data-moves 0. Control case: s=9007199254740993,0 (unsafe input, so Big from the start) works.
findings.specRef: SPEC 4.0 Long numbers; 6.6 Validation (entries up to 40 digits are valid); CLAUDE.md Numbers rule; instruction 5.9 ('If a typed start leaves the safe range, reload with Big')
findings.proposedFix: In stringView, catch EngineOverflow and recompute on bigBoard(board) with BigInt entries, as fireText does. Use the two-ends path whenever any entry of the line can pass 2^53 (|mu_j| + |mu_i|*max|C_ji| > MAX_SAFE). Add unit and e2e tests with s=5,9007199254740990 and s=1,9007199254740991.

findings.what: The tool's own 'no long task when E6 is picked' test is flaky at low load, and the cause is the tool's work at the pick, not the machine. The 'relations' step runs chevalleySerre on the main thread for E6 node 1 (27 positions, 204 records). With the processor slowed four times it takes 37 to 55 ms (median about 45 ms), so roughly 1 run in 8 crosses 50 ms. Two other steps sit close to the budget: mounting the string panel (shell-string: Board, text) took 26 to 66 ms, and the layout of the orbit SVG layers took 40 to 46 ms. The second of these explains the rarer E7 failure, where the relation list is already in the worker. RELATIONS_MAIN_MAX = 27 counts positions but ignores rank: A8 node 1 has 9 positions but 368 relations, and its relations step took 30 to 50 ms at 4x (one long task of 50 ms).
findings.evidence: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=... npx playwright test -c scratch/playwright.config.ts T12.spec.ts -g 'no long task' --repeat-each=10, two batches (load 1.1, then 1.0 to 2.4): E6 failed 2/10 ([1569+58], [1398+63]) then 0/10; E7 0/10 and 0/10. Baseline full suite (load 0.9 to 1.4): E6 failed with a 64 ms task and E7 with a 50 ms task. Untraced instrumented runs (scratch specs/trace.spec.ts, TRACE=0, load 0.4 to 1.0): E6 1/10 with a 56 ms task, whose MutationObserver record [1367] '+out:relation-verdict ... +out:all-relations' places it in the relations step; E7 1/10 with a 50 ms task between '+out:orbit-graph' [1365] and '+panel:matrices' [1473], with no DOM change of the tool's in it, so a rendering task. Overall at load about 1: E6 4/31 failed (56, 58, 63, 64 ms) and E7 2/31 (50, 50 ms). Light traces (devtools.timeline only, tasks-light.mjs): the E6 relations-step TimerFire tasks were 42.1, 55.0, 49.2, 38.9, 37.6, 48.4, 36.9, 53.2 ms. CPU profile of that task: spMul (pr), parseKey (dr), spAdd (mr), spComm (Q) and chevalleySerre (Cr) in src.DfUwg-4O.js, plus GC. E7 traced long tasks were Layout 33 to 43 ms after the orbit vertices or edges were inserted, and a 66 ms TimerFire for '+panel:string'. A8 node 1 relations step: 50.1 and 30.6 ms.
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.6 Main-thread work; E-9; instruction 5.12 and 6 ('switching to E7 node 7 causes no long task')
findings.proposedFix: Bound the main-thread relation list by the work, not by positions: for example size × (6n²−2n) at most what E6 costs at 1x divided by 4. That sends E6 nodes 1 and 6 and every rank-8 list to the worker, or splits chevalleySerre over several tasks per (i, j) once P5-A1 offers a one-relation form. Split the shell-string step: mount Board in one task and the History, text and form in later ones. Give the orbit SVG a contain or content-visibility box so its layout is not one long frame.

findings.what: Known residual, recorded by MERGE as awaiting the owner. Picking a node of 1120 or 1792 positions on B8, C8 or D8 produces long tasks even at full speed: reading the worker's reply of 368 relation checks with both sides takes 53 to 135 ms. At 4x every pick has 3 to 6 long tasks of 50 to 250 ms: minusculeMatrices (on the main thread by E-9 rule 1), the orbitGraph step, signedMoves and the reply.
findings.evidence: scratch specs/trace.spec.ts, PICK=node TRACE=0, cases B8:4,5,6, C8:4,5, D8:4,5,6. RATE=1 (24 runs): 13 runs with one long task of 53 to 135 ms (for example D8-6 [4956+135], ending just before the verdict mutation at 5096). RATE=4 (16 runs): all 16 had long tasks, between 50 and 250 ms (for example B8-5: 161 during the build steps, 64, 109 in the orbit step, and 175 just before the verdict at 6270).
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.6 ('No engine call on the main thread may become a long task'); E-9 rule 1; open question in the P5-A2 report
findings.proposedFix: Owner decision: either size E-9 rule 1 for minusculeMatrices by work, so these orbits go to the worker, or accept and record the exception. In any case, ask P5-A1 for a verdicts-only or one-relation form of chevalleySerre, so that the worker's reply is small.

findings.what: A configured instance with board E7 and node 7 (lesson M8 beat 4 in the plan) computes the whole relation list on the main thread while it hydrates. This is the call the tool sends to the worker after a pick, because it takes about 56 ms at 4x. The build-time result is not reused: every engine call of the configured state runs again in the hydration task.
findings.evidence: Scratch pages dev/t12-e7.astro and dev/t12-a2.astro in a scratch copy of the worktree, with <T12RepresentationBuilder client:idle id='r1' board='E7' node={7}/>, specs/hydrate.spec.ts at 4x, 4 runs each. The hydration task was 363 to 495 ms for E7 against 193 to 264 ms for A2. A full trace of the E7 hydration task (808 ms traced) shows the innermost page frame chevalleySerre (REP_ENGINE wrapper) in 134 of 1577 samples, about 69 ms.
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.6; E-9 ('where a default would need it, the result is computed at build time and shipped as data')
findings.proposedFix: Pass the configured state's relation verdicts (or the whole list) from the server render as island data. Or compute the configured list in a task after hydration, showing 'checked in the background' as the worker path already does.

findings.what: Test gaps found by mutation. With the row and column headers reversed against the entries ('basis-headers'), both suites pass, although the basis-order trap is exactly what the instruction asks the headers to prove. With the relations exported as positions instead of labels ('labels-export'), both suites pass: the unit check toContainEqual({relation:'ef', i:1, j:1}) is also met by the position record of labels 2,2, and the e2e test checks only the length. Several acceptance lines of the instruction have no test: A-2 on a string-board node, a picker, a relation control and a History button with elementFromPoint (only a matrix box is checked); A-8 with no draggable element and the slider scrubbed by arrow keys; overlap of node hit boxes at 320 px; acting from a scrubbed position discarding the later moves; the long-number table view and the words 'more than 2000'; msub in the Serre formula; verdict and string positions after Copy link. I checked each of these by hand and the behaviour is right.
findings.evidence: scratch mutate.py and unit-mutations.sh on a scratch copy: verdict-lookup, basis-export, transpose, grid-threshold, labels-code, string-direction and in-orbit each made 1 to 6 unit tests fail; verdict-component failed the server-render test. basis-headers and labels-export: 'Tests 42 passed (42)'. Build A (verdict-component, basis-headers, string-direction, labels-export), T12.spec.ts without the timing pair: 4 failed (D4, string viewer, G2, flip), all attributable to verdict and direction. Build B (grid-threshold, labels-code): 4 failed (D4, E6 grids, G2, Copy link). My scratch ui.spec.ts confirmed the untested behaviours: focus outline 'solid rgb(0, 114, 178) 3px' with hitOk true on all five controls; slider by ArrowLeft and Home; 0 draggable elements; 0 overlaps; data-moves 2 after scrubbing and firing; table text contains the 20 digits; 2 msub and 1 msup.
findings.specRef: COMMON 4.3; instruction section 6 (A-2, A-8, A-11, History strip, Long numbers, A-12); 9 Traps 'Row is the image'
findings.proposedFix: Assert the row headers against golden weights_dynkin_labels (A2 node 1: '1: (1, 0)', '2: (0, −1)', '3: (−1, 1)'). Assert every exported relation equals the engine list mapped through toLabels (for example a record with i 2 on A2 exists only in labels). Add the missing e2e tests listed above.

findings.what: For four nodes that are not minuscule but whose orbits are built (C5 node 5, C6 node 6, C7 node 7, C8 node 8; 32 to 256 positions), the default relation ef:i,i holds. The tool therefore opens on such a node with the verdict 'equal'. The plan's rule was 'the first failing check ... so that the tool shows a failing relation on load'. The agent changed it for orbits above 27 positions, whose relation list comes from the worker, and recorded the change.
findings.evidence: python3 scratch/ef-default.py over every built non-minuscule node above 27 positions: 'ef:i,i holds on 4 nodes: C5:5(32) C6:6(64) C7:7(128) C8:8(256)'; it fails on the other 62.
findings.specRef: instruction 5.6 default relation; SPEC 4 T12 ('the tool shows the failure otherwise')
findings.proposedFix: When the worker's list arrives and the reader has not picked a relation, move to the first failing check. Or choose the default from a cheap engine check of one relation.

findings.what: The table view's board buttons print negative numbers with an ASCII hyphen-minus ('-1'). SPEC 6.3 requires a true minus sign; T01's table uses Frac, which prints one.
findings.evidence: scratch ui.spec.ts: after firing node 1 on the default, the first table button reads '-1'. The repository's own T12.spec.ts:438 expects toHaveText('-1').
findings.specRef: SPEC 6.3 ('with a true minus sign'); 4.0 Signs
findings.proposedFix: Render the value with Frac, or with the tool's `shown()` helper, which uses the true minus sign and keeps the exact digits.

findings.what: Download data leaves out tables that the screen shows: the layer of each orbit position and the orbit's edges (shown in the figure and in the table view's 'Layer' column), and the two sides of the relation shown (only {relation, i, j, holds} is exported).
findings.evidence: keys of derived in the downloaded JSON (math/reps.json): node, construction, minuscule, orbitSize, built, dimension, explanation, basis, E, F, H, moves, signedMoves, relations, relation, string, positions, drawBound. There is no layer, depth, edges, left or right.
findings.specRef: SPEC 6.6 Data export ('the derived tables shown on screen (positions, roots, edges, matrices)')
findings.proposedFix: Add orbit: [{ basisIndex, position, layer }] and edges: [[from, to, node label]] (when drawn), and the chosen relation's left and right as [row, column, value] lists.

findings.what: Relation node labels are read by indexing the sorted label list with a position (labels[relationRef.i]) instead of through toLabels. This is harmless on named boards, but it breaks the rule that only toLabels and toPositions convert.
findings.evidence: source: `const relationI = $derived(relationRef === null ? nodeLabel : labels[relationRef.i]!);`, where labels = labelOrder(anyBoard).
findings.specRef: SPEC 5.1 E-7; CLAUDE.md conventions ('Only toLabels / toPositions convert')
findings.proposedFix: Use labelOf(anyBoard, relationRef.i) (and the same for j), which goes through toLabels.

After a move the bar holds w=1.2.3.4 with all the other keys; undo writes it back; a relation pick writes q; the matrix-node picker writes nothing. After picking E7 the bar is ?z=1&g=E7&c=n&s=0,0,0,0,0,0,1&w=&k=7&q=ef:7,7. The 22 invalid values give the notice. Scrubbing to 1 and firing gives data-moves 2, and redo does nothing.
notes: The agent's report and the MERGE entry already disclose the 27-position bound, the B8/C8/D8 residual (open question to the owner) and the RelationFormula component; findings 2 and 3 are the measured consequences.

Tracing with the CPU profiler inflates task times by about 15 to 30%. Failure rates come from untraced runs; the per-step durations come from light traces (devtools.timeline only) and from MutationObserver records matched to long-task times.
The hydration of a configured default A2 island is itself one task of 193 to 264 ms at 4x (scratch page). Lab TBT is GATE's job and was not measured.

At 320 px the string viewer's node buttons are 39 px on E8 and D8 and 34 px on B8 (A-7 lists 43 and 38 for a 320 px box), because the board sits inside the panel's padding. That is still at least 24 px with no overlap.

These are shared conventions, not T12 defects: History keeps redo enabled at every cursor; a reset announces 'Undid move 1. Numbers now ...' as T01 does; table-view buttons carry data-table-node and data-table-board rather than data-node.
